seo.title: About the Hawza
seo.description: The story of Imam (AJ) Center – Paris: why the first comprehensive Shi'a hawza in France was established, how it teaches, who leads it, and the institutes it supports across Africa and Europe.

hero.title: A hawza rooted in Paris and open to the wider Francophone world.
hero.description: Imam (AJ) Center – Paris exists to prepare students, preachers, and teachers who can serve France, Europe, Africa, and the wider French-speaking world with language fluency, sound religious grounding, and a contemporary sense of responsibility.

intro.eyebrow: Why a hawza in the West
intro.title: A duty that cannot be carried at a distance.
intro.pullQuote: Hawza education is a collective obligation for scholars in the historic centres of learning. For religious scholars in certain Western and European countries, it becomes an individual one.
paragraphs: While hawza education is considered a collective obligation (farḍ kifāyah) for scholars living in Islamic countries and in historic centres of learning such as Najaf al-Ashraf and Karbala al-Muqaddasah, it becomes an individual obligation (farḍ ʿayn) for religious scholars in certain Western and European countries.

This is particularly true in a culturally and intellectually diverse country like France, where freedom of thought has reached an exceptional level. The administration of Imam (AJ) Center – Paris therefore considers it a personal religious duty to undertake this mission.
The French arena is of tremendous importance at every level. It is essential that Shi'a Muslims make a positive contribution to French society and enrich its social fabric.

France also serves as a gateway — not only to the Maghreb and to Africa, where many people have embraced the teachings of the Ahl al-Bayt (peace be upon them), but to all French-speaking countries, many of which maintain strong cultural ties with France.

overview.title: Why this hawza was established, and why its presence matters.
overview.description: The hawza was shaped around a clear conviction: in countries like France, where intellectual and cultural diversity is especially strong, religious learning must be present, accessible, and able to speak with clarity to the societies around it.

cards.title: A needed responsibility
cards.description: For Muslim communities living in France and across Europe, serious religious learning cannot remain distant. The hawza was established as a local response to that responsibility, helping scholarship take root where people actually live, ask, teach, and serve.

cards.title: Established in Paris
cards.description: During 2002, Ayatollah Shaykh Ismail al-Khaliq began teaching traditional hawza sciences in Paris. In 2012 those study circles were formally organized under the name Imam (AJ) Center – Paris.

cards.title: The first of its kind
cards.description: This hawza is regarded as the first comprehensive Shi'a seminary in France, established to educate followers of the Ahl al-Bayt — and indeed Muslims generally. No previous hawza in France had been established with such breadth and inclusiveness.

cards.title: Nearly half a century of experience
cards.description: Shaykh Ismail al-Khaliq brings close to fifty years of experience in hawza education, and has carried out missionary and educational work in Iraq, Syria, Lebanon, Canada, Africa, Pakistan, and many other countries.

objectives.title: What this hawza sets out to do.
objectives.description: The Center responds to a practical gap: many Europeans are unable to travel to the traditional seminaries of the Islamic world, and Western Muslim communities need scholars who can teach in the languages spoken around them.
items: Train preachers who are integrated into Western society and fluent in local languages.
Provide foundational hawza education in the heart of Europe, in Paris, for those who cannot travel to the traditional seminaries.
Prepare religious scholars capable of preaching and teaching in Western languages in addition to Arabic.
Give students introductory hawza studies that prepare them for advanced specialization, should they later choose to continue at the Najaf Seminary.
objectives.noteDescription: The Center deliberately avoids political involvement. It prohibits the use of its platforms to promote political organizations or to engage in disputes between different groups.

distinctives.title: Two commitments that set the Center apart.
distinctives.description: Its faculty includes highly distinguished scholars, but what distinguishes the Center most is the range of languages it teaches in and the practical shape of what it teaches.

items.title: Multilingual education
items.description: It is the only hawza in the world offering instruction in several languages, so students can study in the language they actually live and preach in.

items.title: Practical curriculum
items.description: Although its faculty includes highly distinguished scholars led by Ayatollah Shaykh Ismail al-Khaliq, the curriculum emphasizes the real needs of Muslims living in Europe, the West, and Africa. Rather than focusing on abstract theoretical debates, it prioritizes the practical religious knowledge Muslims need in contemporary society.

methodology.title: Traditional study, delivered three ways.
methodology.description: The Center follows the traditional hawza curriculum while adapting it to the needs of students living in Western societies. In-person study remains the primary method, but modern technology and distance learning extend the same teaching far beyond Paris.

channels.title: In-person in Paris
channels.description: The primary method of instruction, following the traditional hawza curriculum in the Center's own classrooms.

channels.title: Online and distance learning
channels.description: Courses delivered remotely so students throughout both the East and the West can benefit from hawza education.

channels.title: Affiliated seminaries in Africa
channels.description: In-person classes at the Center's affiliated institutes, taught in local African languages alongside Arabic.

programs.title: Traditional study, adapted to the needs of students in Western societies.
programs.description: Recognizing that many students have careers, university studies, and family responsibilities, the Center has developed two educational tracks alongside a dedicated teacher-training programme.

tracks.title: Religious education programs (part-time)
tracks.description: Educational and cultural courses designed to strengthen the religious identity of Muslims, intended for students who cannot dedicate themselves to full-time hawza studies because of work or university commitments.
points: Covers the Holy Qur'an, jurisprudence (fiqh), Islamic beliefs (ʿaqidah), and ethics.
Includes the biography of the Prophet and the Ahl al-Bayt, Islamic history, and other foundational Islamic sciences.
Graduates receive a certificate qualifying them to teach in local Islamic schools, mosques, and Islamic centers.

tracks.title: Full-time hawza program
tracks.description: For students who wish to devote themselves entirely to religious studies, following the traditional hawza curriculum with minor adaptations suited to Muslims living in the West.
points: An intensive program lasting five years.
Provides an organized route into deeper religious specialization.
Graduates are academically prepared to continue advanced studies at the Hawza in Najaf al-Ashraf.

weekendSchools.title: Training teachers for weekend Islamic schools
weekendSchools.description: As Muslim populations continue to grow in Europe and North America, there is an increasing need for qualified teachers who can educate Muslim children. This programme is distinct from the hawza's scholar-training track: it specifically prepares educators to teach children in Western societies.
points: Islamic subjects: jurisprudence (fiqh), beliefs (ʿaqidah), ethics, and Arabic language.
Classroom management and effective communication skills.
Prepares teachers for Saturday and Sunday Islamic schools across Western communities.

founder.title: Half a century of scholarship, service, and openness.
founder.description: Ayatollah Shaykh Ismail al-Khaliq is among the most prominent Shi'a religious scholars in the West, with a missionary experience spanning more than four decades.
founder.name: Ayatollah Shaykh Ismail al-Khaliq
founder.photoAlt: Portrait of Ayatollah Shaykh Ismail al-Khaliq
paragraphs: He was born in 1957 and grew up in Karbala, Iraq, in the vicinity of the shrine of the Master of Martyrs (peace be upon him).

He began his religious studies in the Hawza of holy Karbala under a select group of its scholars, including Ayatollah Shaykh Mujtaba al-Lankarani, Ayatollah Shaykh Muhammad al-Gharawi, his grandfather Ayatollah Shaykh Muhammad Ibrahim al-Khaliq, and his father Ayatollah Shaykh Muhammad Ali al-Khaliq.

He moved between the hawzas of Karbala and Najaf al-Ashraf until he completed Kifayat al-Usul, and was examined in the advanced levels (al-suṭuh al-ʿulya) by an examination committee composed of Shaykh al-Ha'iri, Shaykh al-Rashti, Shaykh al-Kalbasi, and other scholars — he was thirteen years old at the time.

He then journeyed to the Hawza of Najaf al-Ashraf and sat for an examination in al-Makasib, al-Rasa'il, and al-Kifaya before Grand Ayatollah Sayyid Abu al-Qasim al-Khoei (may Allah sanctify his secret). Following this, he joined the advanced jurisprudence studies (bahth al-kharij) of Ayatollah Sayyid al-Khoei, Ayatollah Sayyid Muhammad al-Ruhani, and Ayatollah Sayyid al-Khomeini.

As oppressive and criminal practices intensified against men of thought, religion, and culture, he was forced, along with some other scholars, to leave Iraq. He travelled between Iran, Pakistan, Syria, and Lebanon. In Pakistan he attained the degree of al-Fadil al-Arabi, ranking first at the national level.

In addition to his elevated religious education in the hawza, he completed his academic studies and obtained a Master's degree from the Arab University in Beirut. He remains deeply committed to the cultural and scientific advancement of the Ummah, working tirelessly to establish schools, hawzas, mosques, libraries, and a university in the regions of the Alawite and Druze communities.

After passing the age of forty, he relocated to the West to begin a cultural, religious, and educational project, taking into account the unique characteristics, cultures, and languages of those countries. He established projects for orphans in Canada and Europe, as well as schools for children to teach the Holy Qur'an, ethics, and the Prophetic biography.

As a result of his extensive engagement in scholarly, cultural, intellectual, and social roles across many countries of the East and West, he became fluent in the languages of the nations he lived in. This wealth of experience gave him a deep understanding of diverse cultures and religions, which facilitated his cultural projects, including interfaith dialogue and rapprochement efforts in the Middle East, Canada, and France.

Carrying a deep concern for elevating the standing of Muslims in the West — so that Muslims might keep pace with their French compatriots in intellectual and civilizational advancement — he began, around 2014, the project of establishing a university: a cultural, educational, and religious project conducted in both Arabic and French, to which he devotes great attention.

He is known for a distinctive approach that combines the preservation of heritage and authenticity on one hand with openness to other cultures on the other, and he possesses a refined humane spirit. He believes strongly in institutional work, continues to carry out his guiding role for Muslims in Paris and throughout France, Britain, and Belgium, and delivers his advanced jurisprudence lessons (bahth al-kharij) to his students in the hawza. He also has writings that remain in manuscript form.

members.name: Shaykh Dr. Mustafa al-Khaliq
members.bio: Originally from France and now based in London, he began hawza studies in Qom in 1999 and studied there for nine years, specializing in jurisprudence, the principles of jurisprudence, Arabic language and grammar, theology, Islamic history, Qur'anic interpretation, and Islamic ethics. He later continued studying with hawza teachers online while remaining active in various European countries. He holds a Bachelor's degree in Foreign Languages and Civilizations from the University of Paris 8 (Saint-Denis), a Master's in Linguistics from Sorbonne Nouvelle, and a PhD in Imami Islamic Ethics from the École Pratique des Hautes Études (EPHE) in Paris. He is currently Imam of the Al-Khoei Centre in London, having previously served as Imam of the Islamic Centre of Swansea in Wales for five years. He has been active in religious outreach for more than twenty-three years — in France and Belgium, for fourteen years in Canada, notably Montreal and Vancouver, and for the past five years in the United Kingdom.
works: The Mystical Dimension of Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him)

members.name: Shaykh Dr. Fares al-Khatib
members.bio: An advanced jurisprudence (bahth al-kharij) student at the Hawza of Najaf al-Ashraf, attending the lessons of Ayatollah Shaykh Baqir al-Irawani. He is a professor and graduate-level instructor in jurisprudence, the principles of jurisprudence, and Qur'anic studies, and a university professor in Iraq who teaches Arabic-language courses for the Center. As a Husayni orator he delivers sermons in numerous European countries and most cities of Iraq. He has published more than fifty research papers in peer-reviewed and non-peer-reviewed academic journals across various fields of Islamic studies, in both Arabic and English.
works: Specialized books in comparative jurisprudence (fiqh muqaran)

capabilities.title: News & announcements
capabilities.description: Publish official notices with dates, categories, summaries and full detail pages.

capabilities.title: Events
capabilities.description: Document lectures, ceremonies, academic sessions and upcoming activities.

capabilities.title: Media galleries
capabilities.description: Attach approved photographs to activity pages without mixing them into the academic content system.

capabilities.title: Search & archive
capabilities.description: Future updates can be filtered by year, category and keyword as the archive grows.

studentPortal.title: Student Portal
studentPortal.description: Secure access area for enrolled learners and approved digital learning resources.

copy.title: Your learning space
copy.description: The student portal will bring enrolled courses, recorded lessons, progress and approved learning resources into one secure area.
copy.signedOutTitle: Sign in to your student account
copy.signedOutDescription: Use your verified account to access academic enrollments, recorded lessons and eligible resources.
copy.securityNote: Sign-in will only be enabled after institutional OAuth credentials, server sessions and role mapping are configured. No password will be collected directly by this website.

sections.title: My Courses
sections.description: Courses and recorded lessons connected to the learner’s enrollment and entitlements.

sections.title: Progress
sections.description: Lesson completion and viewing progress will live here once accounts and the database are connected.

sections.title: My Resources
sections.description: Course attachments and approved learning files, separate from the public Digital Library.

sections.title: Grades
sections.description: Published course grades and approved term averages will appear here when the academic office releases them.

sections.title: Attendance
sections.description: Attendance summaries from approved records will appear here, while detailed editing remains administrative.

accessMap.title: How access works
accessMap.description: The portal supports two distinct paths without mixing academic enrollment with commercial purchases.
accessMap.officialDescription: An admitted student receives access to the courses included in the active academic enrollment. Google Classroom remains the live class and communication space; approved recordings are organized in the portal for catch-up and review.
accessMap.buyerDescription: A visitor who purchases a standalone course receives access only to that purchased course. A purchase never unlocks the full academic program.
accessMap.purchasedLabel: Access comes from a confirmed purchase

signIn.title: Secure sign in
signIn.description: Access your ESPO Paris account and connect it to your academic enrollment when eligible.

copy.title: Your ESPO account
copy.description: Create or access one personal account. The system generates the internal ID automatically and links verified students to their approved academic enrollment.
copy.magicDescription: Use a secure email link when Google sign-in is not suitable. No password needs to be stored by ESPO.
copy.unavailable: This provider is prepared but not active until the production credentials are connected.
copy.securityDescription: Creating an account does not automatically make someone an official hawza student. Academic access is granted only after an approved enrollment is matched or confirmed by administration.
flow: Verify your identity with Google or email.
A secure internal User ID is created automatically.
The verified email is checked against accepted enrollments.
If matched, the enrollment is linked and academic access is activated.
copy.studentNote: Official students receive access from their academic enrollment, not by purchasing each subject.
copy.memberNote: Other users remain regular members and can later access free or individually purchased courses.

support.title: Support the Center
support.description: Contact the administration to learn about the currently available ways to support Imam (AJ) Center – Paris.

copy.title: Contribute to the Center’s educational mission
copy.description: Imam (AJ) Center – Paris continues its educational and community work with the support of benefactors and well-wishers. Contributions can help sustain the Center’s educational mission and its ability to serve learners across countries and languages.
copy.contactDescription: For donations or questions about currently available methods of support, contact the administration directly.
copy.stewardshipDescription: Donation methods are confirmed by the administration. The website does not currently collect card details or process donations automatically.
copy.note: Online donation checkout can be enabled later after the Center approves a payment provider, currencies, receipts and financial procedures.
copy.whatsappMessage: Peace be upon you. I would like to support Imam (AJ) Center – Paris and would like to know the available donation methods.

adminAcademic.title: Academic Control Center
adminAcademic.description: Protected administrative workspace for curriculum, students, results, progression and access.

copy.title: Academic Control Center
copy.description: A protected control layer for student records, curriculum versions, grades, attendance, progression and learning access.
copy.lockedDescription: This route is intentionally locked until real institutional authentication and admin role mapping are connected. No client-side value can unlock it.

modules.title: Students & Enrollment
modules.description: Review matched accounts, active enrollments, statuses and academic placement.

modules.title: Curriculum Management
modules.description: Create curriculum versions, add or deactivate subjects, and assign them to the correct year and semester.

modules.title: Grades & Attendance
modules.description: Enter academic records, then publish only approved grades and attendance summaries to students.

modules.title: Progression Decisions
modules.description: Review recommendations and approve promotion, repetition, holds or program completion.

modules.title: Payments & Entitlements
modules.description: Track contact-price requests, verified offline payments and future online purchases separately from academic enrollment.

modules.title: Enrollment Data Quality
modules.description: Audit Form → language sheet → Central Database imports before they can create or update student records.

modules.title: Audit & Accountability
modules.description: Record who changed grades, enrollment, curriculum, payments and access, with before/after history.

modules.title: Roles & Permissions
modules.description: Keep teachers, academic officers, finance staff, editors and administrators within clearly separated responsibilities.

copy.versioningDescription: Changes for a new academic year are made in a new curriculum version. Existing student records remain attached to the version under which they actually studied.
copy.operationsTitle: One source of truth, controlled changes
copy.operationsDescription: The Central Enrollment Database remains authoritative for student identity and academic placement. Forms, Classroom, Drive and the portal synchronize around it rather than becoming competing databases.
copy.safetyDescription: The system may calculate recommendations and detect data issues, but sensitive actions such as publishing final grades, promoting a student, confirming an offline payment or granting paid access require an authorized server-side action.

content.title: Teacher Gradebook
content.description: A secure, low-friction workspace for entering grades and attendance without exposing the central student database.
content.lockedDescription: This workspace becomes available only after institutional authentication and an assigned teacher role.

workflow.title: Enter grades
workflow.description: Open only the courses and students assigned to you, then enter assessment scores as drafts.

workflow.title: Record attendance
workflow.description: Mark present, absent, excused or late from a fast session roster.

workflow.title: Submit for review
workflow.description: Send completed grade entries to the academic office without publishing them to students.

workflow.title: Publish after approval
workflow.description: Only an academic officer or administrator can release approved results to the Student Portal.

content.storageDescription: In the first phase, protected Google Sheets store academic records behind Apps Script. Teachers use this portal, not raw spreadsheets. The storage can later migrate without changing the interface.
content.safetyDescription: Draft and submitted grades remain invisible to students. Every sensitive change is designed to be attributable to an authorized staff member.

copy.title: Grade Review & Publication
copy.description: A controlled review stage between teacher entry and student visibility. Submitted grades are checked for completeness before academic approval and publication.
copy.lockedDescription: This workspace remains locked until production authentication and authorized staff roles are connected.

steps.title: Receive submissions
steps.description: Teachers submit completed gradebooks for review.

steps.title: Validate records
steps.description: The system checks missing assessments, invalid values, and draft entries.

steps.title: Academic approval
steps.description: An authorized academic officer reviews and approves or returns the batch.

steps.title: Publish to students
steps.description: Only approved records become visible in the Student Portal.

copy.ruleDescription: A batch cannot be published while required assessments are missing or entries remain in draft status.
copy.visibilityDescription: Students only see published results; drafts, returned records, and internal notes remain private.

copy.title: Your academic record
copy.description: A private view of published results, approved term averages, attendance summaries and progression history tied to your official student identity.
copy.lockedDescription: Academic records are private and only become available after a verified account is linked to an accepted enrollment.

cards.title: Term history
cards.description: Published course results remain attached to the academic year and curriculum version in which they were earned.

cards.title: Approved averages
cards.description: Only academically approved term averages are shown. Draft teacher entries never appear here.

cards.title: Attendance summary
cards.description: Approved attendance summaries are visible without exposing internal administrative notes.

copy.privacyDescription: Future curriculum edits never rewrite a student’s previous academic record. Each term remains tied to its original curriculum version and AIC student identity.

copy.title: Term Closing & Progression
copy.description: A controlled end-of-term workflow that turns published results into an academic recommendation, then requires an authorized human decision before the next term is activated.
copy.lockedDescription: Progression decisions remain locked until production authentication and authorized academic roles are connected.

steps.title: Close academic records
steps.description: Confirm that all required grades are published and attendance records are complete.

steps.title: Generate recommendation
steps.description: The system evaluates the current standing and proposes promotion, hold or program completion.

steps.title: Human approval
steps.description: An authorized academic officer approves the recommendation or records an explicit exception.

steps.title: Activate next term
steps.description: After approval, the new semester and course access can be activated while prior history remains immutable.

copy.guardDescription: The system may recommend a next step, but it never advances a student solely because a date changed or a grade was entered. Academic approval is mandatory.
copy.auditDescription: The progression record stores the source term, decision, approver, timestamp and reason so later administrators can reconstruct what happened.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.description: Secure academic and operational notifications for students, teachers and administrators.

content.title: Notifications & action center
content.description: A single place for published results, enrollment updates, review requests, progression decisions, payment confirmations and learning notices. Live delivery activates only after production authentication and persistence are connected.
content.lockedDescription: Notifications are private and role-aware. The production inbox will open only after the account is securely authenticated.
content.inAppDescription: Students, teachers and administrators receive only the updates relevant to their role and records. Unread state is tracked without exposing other users' information.
content.emailDescription: Important events can also be delivered by email through the institution's approved mail provider. Users can keep in-app delivery while disabling non-essential email notices.
content.safetyTitle: No academic result is published by notification alone
content.safetyDescription: A notification reports an already-authorized event. Grade publishing, progression, payment confirmation and access decisions still follow their own protected approval workflows.

copy.title: Enrollment Integrity Center
copy.description: A controlled workspace for auditing the six enrollment sources, repairing the central database, resolving identity mismatches and protecting the AIC student record before portal access is activated.
copy.lockedDescription: Live audit and repair actions remain unavailable until production authentication is connected and the signed-in account is authorized as an enrollment administrator.

cards.title: Source audit
cards.description: Compare Arabic, English, French, Persian, Turkish and Azerbaijani response sheets against the central Applications database.

cards.title: Safe repair
cards.description: Preview missing fields first, then backfill only empty central values while preserving administrator edits and existing AIC IDs.

cards.title: Identity linking
cards.description: Match a verified website account to the existing AIC record by normalized email. Account creation never creates a second student identity.

cards.title: Change control
cards.description: Repairs require an authorized administrator, a signed server request and an explicit apply confirmation. Dry-run is the default.

workflow: Create a backup and run a read-only audit.
Resolve mapping errors in the six source sheets.
Review proposed field repairs and duplicate warnings.
Apply repairs only after explicit administrator confirmation.
Re-run the audit and verify student folder names.
Enable account-to-AIC linking only after data integrity passes.
copy.liveDescription: This control center is designed to inspect first and write second. The production database is never repaired merely because a page was opened.

productionReadiness.title: Production readiness
productionReadiness.body: A gated operational view for enrollment, identity and academic-write activation. No feature is marked ready until the live environment proves it.
productionReadiness.lockedBody: Production authentication is not active yet. This page intentionally reveals no administrative state to anonymous visitors.

academicOperations.title: Academic Operations Console
academicOperations.description: Operational readiness for the academic workspace, staff access, gradebook and controlled publishing.

copy.title: Academic Operations Console
copy.description: A protected operations view for provisioning, authorization, assessment configuration and academic data integrity before live teaching workflows are enabled.
copy.lockedDescription: The console stays locked until production authentication maps this account to an authorized academic role.

cards.title: Workspace provisioning
cards.description: Prepare the six canonical Google Sheets with stable headers, validation rules and operational safeguards.

cards.title: Staff access
cards.description: Assign teachers only to their course offerings and keep review, publishing and administrative permissions separated.

cards.title: Assessment integrity
cards.description: Validate active assessment weights and prevent incomplete or malformed grading structures from going live.

cards.title: Controlled publishing
cards.description: Keep draft, review, approval and publication as separate stages with a permanent audit trail.

copy.footerDescription: The first production architecture uses Vercel, Google Workspace and Apps Script. No dedicated server is required at the current stage.

curriculumControl.title: Curriculum Control Center
curriculumControl.description: Versioned academic-program management for subjects, semesters and future academic years.

copy.title: Curriculum Control Center
copy.description: Manage the academic structure without rewriting history. Draft future curricula, edit subjects before activation, and preserve the exact curriculum each student studied.
copy.lockedDescription: This workspace remains locked until production authentication and academic-officer permissions are active.

principles.title: Edit drafts safely
principles.description: Add, rename, reorder or deactivate subjects only inside a draft curriculum version.

principles.title: Create the next year
principles.description: Clone the current curriculum into a new academic year, then adjust it without altering prior records.

principles.title: Preserve history
principles.description: Activated curricula are immutable. Existing transcripts continue to reflect the curriculum actually studied.

principles.title: Govern changes
principles.description: Activation is a deliberate academic action, protected by validation and role-based permissions.

lifecycle: Create or clone a draft curriculum version.
Review year, semester and subject structure.
Validate codes, ordering and year/semester alignment.
Approve and activate the version for the academic year.
Archive only when it is no longer operational; never rewrite historical records.
copy.controlsDescription: Subject name, code, description, year, semester, display order and active status are administrative data. Future teacher assignment and course delivery remain separate from the immutable curriculum record.

staffAccess.title: Staff Access & Teaching Assignments
staffAccess.description: Controlled staff roles, account lifecycle and teacher-to-course assignments.

copy.title: Staff Access & Teaching Assignments
copy.description: Keep staff identity, academic authority and teaching assignments separate. Administration controls who may enter the system, while the academic officer can assign active teachers only to the course offerings they actually teach.
copy.lockedDescription: Staff identity and role management remains locked until production authentication is active.

roles.title: Teacher
roles.description: Sees assigned course offerings, records attendance, saves draft grades and submits them for review.

roles.title: Academic Officer
roles.description: Assigns teachers to course offerings, reviews academic submissions, publishes results and approves progression.

roles.title: Finance
roles.description: Confirms authorized payments and financial access without receiving academic editing permissions.

roles.title: Editor
roles.description: Maintains approved public content without gaining student-grade or staff-management authority.

roles.title: Administrator
roles.description: Controls staff accounts, role changes, suspensions and the highest-risk system settings.

workflow: Invite or verify the staff member using an institutional or approved email address.
Assign one operational role; do not combine unrelated privileges by convenience.
For teachers, assign only the active course offerings they teach.
Suspend access immediately when duties change or a staff member leaves.
Preserve the audit history of role and assignment changes.
copy.securityDescription: Finance is not treated as a higher teacher role, editors cannot publish grades, and academic officers cannot silently become system administrators. Access is capability-based rather than a simplistic role ranking.

cohortManagement.title: Cohort Management
cohortManagement.description: Manage academic-year cohorts and controlled student rollover without rewriting historical records.

copy.title: Cohorts, progression, and year rollover
copy.description: Prepare each academic year as a controlled cohort linked to one approved curriculum version, while preserving every student’s existing AIC identity and academic history.
copy.lockedDescription: This control surface stays locked until production authentication and academic administrator permissions are active.

principles.title: One cohort per academic cycle
principles.description: Students are grouped by academic year without changing their permanent AIC identity.

principles.title: Advance only after approval
principles.description: A new semester membership is created only after the academic progression decision is approved.

principles.title: History remains immutable
principles.description: Closed cohort memberships stay preserved for transcripts, audits, and later verification.

principles.title: Curriculum stays versioned
principles.description: Each cohort points to an approved curriculum version instead of silently inheriting future changes.

workflow: Close and publish the current term results.
Activate the next curriculum version and academic cohort.
Create next-semester memberships only for eligible students.
Archive prior memberships without deleting grades, attendance, or AIC IDs.
Reconcile Classroom and portal access after the cohort is activated.
copy.safeguardDescription: The system can prepare rollover recommendations in bulk, but it never promotes every student simply because the calendar year changed. Academic approval remains the final gate.

adminContent.title: Content Management
adminContent.description: Manage institutional news, activities, announcements and scheduled reflections.

copy.title: Content & Publishing Center
copy.description: A controlled CMS workspace for publishing, scheduling and maintaining public website content without editing code.
copy.lockedDescription: Sign in with an authorized editor or administrator account to manage website content.
copy.masterDescription: Full authority over publishing, deletion, permissions and global content settings.
copy.editorDescription: Can prepare, edit and schedule content, while final publishing and deletion remain protected.

modules.title: News
modules.description: Create, edit, schedule, publish or archive institutional news.

modules.title: Activities
modules.description: Manage events, reports, galleries and public activity entries.

modules.title: Daily verse / hadith
modules.description: Maintain an approved library of Qurʾanic verses and hadith for daily rotation.

modules.title: Scheduling
modules.description: Plan future publication, expiry and occasion-specific content.

copy.workflowDescription: Draft → Review → Schedule → Publish → Archive. Editors prepare content; the master administrator retains final destructive and publishing authority.
copy.reflectionDescription: Normal approved entries rotate automatically by day. Higher-priority entries can be scheduled for specific occasions and date ranges, with source attribution required.
copy.destructiveDescription: Permanent deletion, final publishing and site-wide settings remain restricted to the master administrator and should be audit logged.

live.liveDescription: This workspace reads and writes institutional website content through the signed Google Apps Script bridge. No public content is fabricated when the bridge is unavailable.
live.noContent: No CMS entries are stored yet.
live.noReflections: No approved-source reflections are stored yet.

adminDashboard.title: Administration Dashboard
adminDashboard.description: Protected administration workspace for ESPO Paris operations.

copy.title: Administration Dashboard
copy.description: A protected command center for website content, academic operations and institutional systems. Only modules permitted for the signed-in role are exposed.
copy.statusDescription: This area is excluded from public navigation and search indexing, and every protected route is checked server-side before rendering.
copy.liveDataDescription: No student, content, library or learning counts are fabricated. Operational metrics appear only after the corresponding production repository is connected and verified.
copy.modulesDescription: Available modules open immediately. Foundation modules are already architected but remain inactive until their production data source is connected.

content.title: Content & Publishing
content.description: Prepare, review, schedule, publish and archive news, activities, announcements and approved daily reflections.

academic.title: Academic Administration
academic.description: Manage curriculum, cohorts, staff assignments, grade review, attendance, progression and academic readiness.

library.title: Digital Library
library.description: Manage institutional books, metadata, covers and controlled PDF access once the digital Drive repository is connected.

learning.title: Learning Platform
learning.description: Manage recorded courses, lessons, attachments and access rules after the learning repository is activated.

people.title: People & Permissions
people.description: Master-admin control for staff identities, roles and administrative access boundaries.

settings.title: Site Settings
settings.description: Master-admin area for verified institutional settings, public contact data and controlled configuration.

adminPeople.title: People & Permissions
adminPeople.description: Master-admin workspace for staff identities, roles and access control.

copy.title: People & Permissions
copy.description: Control staff roles and administrative boundaries from one protected workspace. No live staff directory is fabricated before the production identity source is connected.
copy.masterTitle: Master Admin remains the final authority
copy.masterDescription: Only the Master Admin can assign administrative roles, manage permission boundaries and control high-risk access. Operational staff receive only the capabilities required for their work.
copy.liveTitle: Live identity directory not connected yet
copy.liveDescription: The permission model is active in code, but real invitations and role changes remain disabled until Google authentication and persistent identity storage are activated.

roles.title: Teacher
roles.description: Teaching access for assigned course offerings only.

roles.title: Academic Officer
roles.description: Reviews academic records, progression and academic operations.

roles.title: Finance
roles.description: Finance-specific review without inheriting academic or publishing authority.

roles.title: Content Editor
roles.description: Creates and prepares public content without final administrative control.

roles.title: Master Admin
roles.description: Full institutional administration and permission control.

lifecycle.title: Invite
lifecycle.description: Create a pending identity only after the official email is verified.

lifecycle.title: Activate
lifecycle.description: Assign the minimum role needed and activate access.

lifecycle.title: Suspend
lifecycle.description: Temporarily revoke access without deleting audit history.

lifecycle.title: Depart
lifecycle.description: Close access permanently while preserving historical records.

copy.safetyDescription: Changing a staff role never grants unrelated capabilities. Departed accounts cannot be silently reactivated, and role changes must remain auditable.

adminSettings.title: Site Settings
adminSettings.description: Master-admin workspace for verified public institutional configuration.

copy.title: Site Settings
copy.description: Manage verified public contact information and institutional settings without placing unconfirmed data into the website or search engines.
copy.contactDescription: These values are the confirmed institutional contact channels currently permitted for public use.
copy.pendingDescription: Address, visiting hours and final legal naming remain empty until the institution confirms them.
copy.publishRuleDescription: A setting may be stored as a draft, but unverified institutional information must never be emitted into public pages, metadata or structured data.
copy.persistenceDescription: The settings UI and validation model are ready. Saving live changes is enabled only after authenticated production persistence is connected.

copy.readOnly: Published and archived metadata is read-only. Use the controlled lifecycle actions.
copy.title: Title
copy.author: Author
copy.description: Description

adminLibrary.title: Digital Library Administration
adminLibrary.description: Manage approved library metadata and Drive-backed publication records.

copy.title: Digital Library Administration
copy.description: Review the institution's book catalog and its approved Google Drive references without exposing private storage directly to visitors.
copy.safetyDescription: The website reads metadata through a signed server-to-server bridge. Files remain under the institution-owned digital Google Workspace account.
copy.empty: No live catalog is shown until the digital@espoparis.com bridge is deployed and configured.

adminLearning.title: Learning Platform Administration
adminLearning.description: Manage recorded-learning metadata and academic Drive references.

copy.title: Learning Platform Administration
copy.description: Review recorded lessons and approved course assets while keeping academic access rules separate from public content.
copy.safetyDescription: Published lesson metadata can be exposed safely while student-only and paid assets remain subject to entitlement checks before delivery.
copy.empty: No live lessons are shown until the digital@espoparis.com bridge is deployed and configured.
